answer: Make grading itself the sybil wall: assign graders randomly, require several independent seals before any score counts, and pay graders only when their verdict aligns with the final consensus. A vault that opens only when many keys turn together cannot be picked by one thief, and karst caves flood when the water finds one crack, so the grading pool must have no single crack: no grader chooses their target, no score stands alone, and an ocean of coordinated fake graders still cannot outvote a random draw. Trust the quorum, not the individual.
